subject: Re: Order form redlines - product rights, training use, and feedback escrow
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@avalon.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@avalon.io>, Mark Reeves <mark.reeves@avalon-legal.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form redlines - product rights, training use, and feedback escrow

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal has circulated our preliminary redlines to the Order Form and a short SOW for the proposed feedback-escrow arrangement. The two main asks from our side are: (1) explicit assignment vs. license for model outputs used in our customer-facing product, and (2) a contractual guarantee that Redwood will not use Avalon customer data or outputs to train models without an opt-in.

Mark attached our redlines (Avalon_Redlines_20270615.pdf) and proposed language for a third-party escrow that would allow us to review aggregated feedback artifacts quarterly. We understand Redwood's position on model productization but need a bounded, auditable path for productization decisions.

Can you confirm who on your legal/product teams we should loop in for a redline call tomorrow? Also, if Redwood can propose a short set of compromise language for output ownership (assignment vs. non-exclusive license) and a telemetry/feedback license carveout, that would speed the procurement review.

Best,
Julia

--
Julia Park
Head of Procurement, Avalon Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@avalon.io>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Mark Reeves <mark.reeves@avalon-legal.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines - product rights, training use, and feedback escrow

Julia — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. I’ve looped in Ben (sales lead), Laura (contracts/legal partner), and Olga (privacy/compliance) so we can get aligned quickly.

Quick summary of Redwood's starting position:
- We generally grant customers broad use rights for outputs (non-exclusive, transferable for downstream productization), but we do not typically assign intellectual property in outputs.
- We will not train models on customer data/outputs without an explicit opt-in and contract language to that effect.
- Feedback telemetry is something we can compartmentalize; for Avalon’s use-case we can offer a controlled escrow where aggregated feedback artifacts are made available under audit terms, but escrow details (format, cadence, retention) need to be narrowed.

Action items I’m proposing before a joint call:
1) Redwood to propose two short alternative clauses for output rights: (A) exclusive assignment of customer-generated outputs for the specific product under the Order Form (time-limited), (B) perpetual, non-exclusive, assignable license with attribution and limited sub-licensing.
2) Redwood legal to draft an explicit training-opt-out clause and telemetry handling addendum that references the SOW.
3) Joint call with Avalon legal + procurement + Redwood contracts tomorrow at 2pm PT — confirm if that works.

I’ll attach Redwood’s proposed language in a follow-up in the next hour.

Thanks,
Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@avalon.io>, Mark Reeves <mark.reeves@avalon-legal.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines - product rights, training use, and feedback escrow

Team — attaching Redwood_Proposed_OrderForm_Clause_v3.docx and a short redline summary below. High-level recommendation: aim for option (B) below with a limited productization carveout (12 months exclusivity window + obligation to notify and revenue-share if commercialized). This balances Avalon’s need for product rights with Redwood’s platform and model IP protections.

Proposed compromise (summary):
- Output ownership: Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, assignable license to use, reproduce, and distribute Outputs generated from Customer inputs under the Order Form. Customer may request assignment for specific deliverables where Avalon provides material investment in prompt engineering or training artifacts; Redwood will consider assignment requests on a case-by-case basis governed by a short SOW and a one-time fee.
- Training/data use: Redwood will not use Customer data or Outputs to further train or fine-tune Redwood models without Customer's prior written consent. For telemetry/feedback that is aggregated and de-identified, Redwood may use such data for service improvement, subject to the Data Processing Addendum and an explicit aggregation-only definition.
- Feedback escrow: Redwood agrees to deposit quarterly summaries of aggregated feedback artifacts to a mutually agreed escrow (Feedback-Escrow-SOW.pdf). Avalon will have read-only audit access; technical artifacts containing PII or raw customer prompts will be excluded unless redacted.

Please see the doc for exact clause text. I’ve annotated areas where we’d want Sales to approve potential fees for assignment requests and where Compliance needs to sign off on the retention/PII carveouts.

If everyone’s available, we confirm the 2pm PT call — I’ll stand by to walk through the compromise live.

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Mark Reeves <mark.reeves@avalon-legal.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@avalon.io>, Procurement <procurement@avalon.io>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines - product rights, training use, and feedback escrow

Laura / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. We ran the compromise by Avalon product and procurement; the approach looks workable and the assignment-on-request mechanism is acceptable provided the process and fee schedule are spelled out in the SOW. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Please add an explicit timeline for Redwood’s notification to Avalon if Redwood intends to use aggregated feedback for model improvements (we suggest 30 days notice and an opt-out window).
2) We need more detail in the Feedback-Escrow-SOW around data formats and redaction standards so our security team can validate there’s no re-identification risk.
3) Avalon’s procurement asks that any assignment requests be processed within 60 days of written request (to avoid open hold-ups).

If Redwood can incorporate those three items into the next draft, Avalon’s legal can clear and move to signature this week.

Mark Reeves
Senior Counsel, Avalon Health
